item.title: Differential Effect of Endovascular Treatment in Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: A Distal Secondary Analysis.
item.author: Kurmann C, Fischer U, Rommers N, Brehm A, Aebischer V, Cavalcante F, Campbell BCV, Gralla J, Psychogios MN, Kaesmacher J, DISTAL Investigators.
item.description:
Background Patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion stroke are heterogeneous. Randomized trials show no net benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) over best medical treatment (BMT) alone, which may mask heterogeneity of treatment effect. We used an externally developed machine learning model to predict excellent early neurological outcome (EENO) with BMT alone and examined whether the effect of EVT differed across predicted risk. item.title: Endothelial Cell-Expressed Prion Protein Prnd/Doppel Promotes Long-Term Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
item.author: Wang T, Kim S, Morales JE, McCarty JH.
item.description:
Background Recovery after ischemic stroke is limited by persistent cerebrovascular dysfunction, but the mechanisms regulating vascular repair remain poorly understood. Prnd (Prnd/Doppel) is a prion family protein expressed in the cerebrovascular endothelium during development. We tested the hypothesis that endothelial Prnd promotes vascular repair and functional recovery in the adult brain after stroke. Methods Using middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice, we compared wild-type and Prnd-null mice and evaluated endothelial-specific Prnd overexpression. Functional recovery was assessed by behavioral testing, while infarct volume, brain atrophy, vascular architecture, blood-brain barrier integrity, and macrophage/microglia infiltration were evaluated histologically. item.author: Tanaka K, Coutts SB, Joundi RA, Singh N, Uehara T, Ohara T, Toyoda K, Koga M, Koge J, Bibok MB, Smith EE, Minematsu K, Demchuk AM.
item.description:
Background The ABCD 2 score is widely used to stratify stroke risk after transient neurological events. We aimed to evaluate the association between the ABCD 2 score and the risk of subsequent ischemic stroke among patients with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-positive (DWI+) or DWI-negative (DWI-) findings for the index event. Methods We pooled individual participant data from 3 multicenter cohorts including patients presenting with transient or minor neurological events. Patients presenting with transient neurological symptoms, a normal neurological examination, and available DWI for the index event were included. Associations between the ABCD 2 score and 90-day ischemic stroke risk were analyzed separately in the DWI+ and DWI- groups using logistic regression models adjusted for sex, atrial fibrillation, and study source. item.description:
Background Successful thrombectomy recanalization combined with intraarterial thrombolysis showed potential benefits in achieving excellent outcomes in recent trials, but the results were inconsistent. We performed this study to investigate the efficacy and safety of interarterial thrombolysis in patients stratified by expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) score after thrombectomy. item.title: Comparative Safety and Efficacy of Oral Anticoagulants in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Prior Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized-Controlled Clinical Trials.
item.author: Papageorgiou NM, Palaiodimou L, Theodorou A, Stefanou MI, Panagiotopoulos E, Katsanos AH, Safouris A, Kargiotis O, Sacco S, Turc G, Fischer U, Khatri P, Yaghi S, Tsivgoulis G.
item.description:
Background Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and prior ischemic stroke represent a high-risk population facing competing risks of recurrent thromboembolism and hemorrhagic complications. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended over vitamin K antagonists for stroke prevention in AF, no randomized controlled clinical trial has directly compared individual DOACs to each other in this population. Methods We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized-controlled clinical trials enrolling patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. MEDLINE, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary outcome was any stroke. item.author: D'Anna L, Prandin G, De Santis F, Gabriele F, Ornello R, Cascio Rizzo A, Sessa M, Schwarz G, Tortorella R, Pantoni L, Mele F, Scopelliti G, Cova I, Casolla B, Gulla M, Diallo SM, Baude M, González L, Rigual R, Fuentes B, Caliandro P, Zauli A, Reale G, Abdelalim A, Ahmed S, Ali Ismail S, Zhang L, Latimer T, Elboghday M, Ferrari F, Mazzacane F, Fonseca AC, Antunes B, Piscaglia MG, Balducci G, Miserocchi LM, Zedde M, Elsayed AE, Desai G, Jaffar M, Banerjee S, Polymeris A, Sacco S, Foschi M.
item.description:
Background Patients with atrial fibrillation who experience ischemic stroke despite oral anticoagulation (breakthrough stroke) remain at high risk of recurrent vascular events and death. Although inflammation has been associated with thromboembolic risk, its prognostic role in breakthrough stroke remains unclear. We investigated whether a composite inflammatory burden index was associated with adverse outcomes after breakthrough ischemic stroke.
